# datadog_derived_metric (Resource)

Provides a Datadog derived metric resource computed from a formula and metric queries. Managing derived metrics requires the Manage Tags for Metrics permission.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a derived metric that combines two metric queries
resource "datadog_derived_metric" "cpu_total" {
  name = "custom.cpu.total"
  definition = {
    formula = "a + b"
    queries = [
      {
        name        = "a"
        data_source = "metrics"
        query       = "avg:system.cpu.user{*}"
      },
      {
        name        = "b"
        data_source = "metrics"
        query       = "avg:system.cpu.system{*}"
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `definition` (Attributes) The definition of a derived metric as a formula over one or more queries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--definition))
- `name` (String) Caller-assigned name sent as the create ID. After import, the first apply adopts the configured name through an update using the canonical API ID, without replacing the resource. Once the name is stored in state, changing it replaces the resource. String length must be at least 1.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--definition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `definition`

Required:

- `formula` (String) The formula that combines the queries into the value of the derived metric.
- `queries` (Attributes List) The list of queries referenced by the formula. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--definition--queries))

<a id="nestedatt--definition--queries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `definition.queries`

Required:

- `data_source` (String) The data source that the query is run against.
- `name` (String) The name used to reference this query from the formula.
- `query` (String) The query string executed against the data source.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Derived metrics can be imported using their name, e.g.
terraform import datadog_derived_metric.cpu_total "custom.cpu.total"
```
